Hi Alex / Marissa —

Quick note from Security/Compliance: happy to support and here's what we can commit to in the timeline.

1) SOC2: we can share a redacted SOC2 Type II report for review (attached: SOC2-TypeII-Report-Redwood.pdf). Full access to the control environment can be provided under NDA.
2) Retention recommendations: for PHI workloads we typically recommend:
   - Raw inputs (request payload): configurable by customer — defaults we recommend: 30 days (hosted) / customer-configurable up to 90 days.
   - Inference outputs: configurable — many customers keep 30 days unless needed for audit.
   - Audit logs / request traces: retained 365 days by default; export options available (S3/secure transfer).
3) Logging & audit trails: token-level and request-level logging available; logs include request timestamp, model/version, route, and anonymized metadata by default. For PHI workloads we can enable stricter retention and full request-id tracing tied to audit events.
4) Key management & isolation: KMS integrations supported (AWS KMS, Google KMS). For customers requiring HSM-backed keys or full network isolation we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated pools.
5) PHI handling & HIPAA: Redwood can operate under a BAA. Execution of a BAA and legal review will be required before production when PHI is in scope. We can send a standard BAA template for redlining.

Attachments: SOC2-TypeII-Report-Redwood.pdf (redacted), Security-Questionnaire-Redwood.xlsx (completed sections).

If HealthInsight can confirm the desired retention window (30/60/90) and whether they require Private deployment, we can update the MAP and move to BAA next steps.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
